title: Target-Decoy Statistical Foundations
markdown:
## What this covers

This chapter covers the statistical formulation of peptide-spectrum match (PSM) evaluation in shotgun proteomics. It formalizes PSM scoring as a two-component mixture model, defines the Posterior Error Probability (PEP) and False Discovery Rate (FDR), and shows how the competitive Target-Decoy Approach (TDA) estimates these quantities empirically.

## Mixture Models for PSM Scores

Shotgun mass spectrometry assigns observed experimental spectra to theoretical peptides stored in a sequence database. Let $x$ denote a search engine score for a given peptide-spectrum match (PSM), oriented such that larger values of $x$ represent a better match between theoretical and observed spectra.

Because any search returns a mixture of correct and incorrect assignments, the overall distribution of target PSM scores $f(x)$ is modeled as a two-component mixture:

$$ f(x) = \pi_0 f_0(x) + (1 - \pi_0) f_1(x) $$

where:
- $f_0(x)$ is the probability density function of scores for incorrect (bad) PSMs.
- $f_1(x)$ is the probability density function of scores for correct (good) PSMs.
- $\pi_0$ is the marginal probability that a randomly chosen PSM is incorrect (the fraction of bad hits in the entire set of returned target matches).
